blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A planner fills a $12M envelope by sorting projects by value per $k and taking each one that still fits. The model funds a different set that is worth more. How can that happen?

options.text: The best mix can leave out a high-ratio project so the rest use the money
options.says: Right: greedy takes a project and then cannot use what is left; a different mix fills the envelope better.

options.text: The greedy fill spends past the envelope when two projects tie on ratio
options.says: Greedy takes a project only if it still fits, so it never spends past the envelope.

options.text: The model ranks the projects by value per $k, in a different sort order
options.says: The model maximizes the sum of values within the budget row; it does not sort by ratio at all.

options.text: Greedy finds the best fill, and the model differs from it only by rounding
options.says: The page shows greedy $208k short at $15M; the gap is a worse choice of projects, not rounding.

origin.section: A Sort by Value per Dollar Is Not the Best Fill

questions.stem: A teammate writes a new test for step 01: solve a request, then assert only that the funded projects' capex is within the envelope. What does this test show when run on the skeleton in steps/00?

options.text: It fails on the skeleton, which shows that a model has been added
options.says: The stub funds nothing, and an empty plan respects any budget, so the test passes there.

options.text: It raises on the skeleton, since the stub has no plan for it to read
options.says: The stub returns a Plan with status 'not solved'; it never raises.

options.text: It passes on the skeleton, so it cannot tell the two versions apart
options.says: Right: an empty plan fits every budget; the lesson's test also checks the status and that something is funded.

options.text: It fails on the skeleton, since an empty plan has no capex to sum up
options.says: The capex of an empty plan is 0, which is within any envelope, so the test passes.

origin.section: Each Test Checks What the Planners Asked, on Data Small Enough to Solve by Hand

questions.stem: The export marks project Q as a must-do, and Q has a low value. What does the step-01 planner do with Q?

options.text: It refuses the export, since the column is one it has no use for
options.says: The loader reads the columns it uses and ignores the rest; it refuses only duplicate ids.

options.text: It treats Q like any project, since the loader never reads that column
options.says: Right: in this version the must-do flag is in the export and nothing reads it.

options.text: It funds Q first, since a must-do outranks any value the others have
options.says: Step 01 has no must-do rule; Q competes on value like every other project.

options.text: It warns in the report, since the column marks a rule it cannot keep
options.says: Nothing reads the column, so the gap goes unnoticed; the business-rules step's tests catch it.

origin.section: Design Note: Read Only the Columns You Use

concepts: what the first version does with columns it does not read
why sorting by ratio can miss the best fill
what a test that only checks the budget proves
